posts.heading: October 9, 2026
posts.text:
The station logged 218 feeder visits and 23 species. Eastern Phoebe and Tufted Titmouse remained the primary callers, with the Phoebe accounting for over half of all audio detections. Tufted Titmouse also dominated visual records, with 135 confident visits observed throughout the day.

A Brown Thrasher returned to the log after a seven-day absence, last recorded on October 2. The station’s audio source underwent frequent changes between microphones on October 9, including switches between pi, c120, and pi-mic.

The visual window opened early with a Northern Cardinal recorded 11 minutes before sunrise and closed with a House Sparrow seen 13 minutes before sunset. The day concluded with a total of 18 species heard and 14 seen.

posts.heading: October 8, 2026
posts.text:
Yesterday recorded 24 species compared to the past week’s average of 19.4. The day had 140 feeder visits versus the weekly average of 257.3, while audio detections totaled 404, exceeding the recent norm of 326.7. Eastern Phoebe, Eastern Towhee, and Carolina Wren maintained their presence throughout the day. A male Rose-breasted Grosbeak perched on a black metal feeder stand in the grassy yard, consistent with its appearance on four of the last seven days.

The Eastern Bluebird returned after an 11-day absence, having last been recorded on September 27. This bird was detected once during the evening hours.

With a high of 24.889 C and no precipitation, the station saw a stable mix of seen and heard species, totaling 10 birds detected by both methods. Tufted Titmice and Carolina Chickadees were the most frequent visitors at the feeders, with 51 and 22 confident sightings respectively. The Northern Cardinal was the last visual record, appearing one minute after sunset.

posts.heading: October 7, 2026
posts.text:
The station recorded 19 species and 118 feeder visits, making it the quietest day of the past week compared to the recent average of 266.6 visits. While species diversity matched the weekly mean, the low traffic volume stands out against the heavier counts seen earlier in the period. Most regulars, including Tufted Titmice, Carolina Chickadees, and Northern Cardinals, maintained their consistent presence at the feeders.

Audio detection totaled 367 events, exceeding the weekly average despite the drop in visual visits. Eastern Phoebes and Eastern Towhees accounted for the majority of these detections.

Two raptors, a Red-shouldered Hawk and an American Kestrel, were heard during the day, both of which have been present at the station in the recent past. The Pileated Woodpecker was also detected, continuing its intermittent appearances. No new species were recorded visually or audibly that were not previously established at this station, maintaining the known baseline of local avian residents.

posts.heading: October 6, 2026
posts.text:
The station recorded 137 feeder visits and 21 species, a quieter day than the previous week's average of 293 visits. Despite the lower visit count, the variety of species remained steady, matching the weekly average of 21.1. Longtime regulars such as Tufted Titmice, Carolina Chickadees, and Eastern Towhees continued to dominate both the visual and audio logs.

Several species were absent from today's list, including the Brown Thrasher, Eastern Screech-Owl, and Ruby-throated Hummingbird, which have been present earlier in the week. In contrast, the American Kestrel was recorded for the first time at this station. This new auditory detection aligns with the installation of the new woodpecker brick cage-feeder earlier in the week, marking the first confident visual and audio record of this species at the site.

The day's activity was spread across the hours, with the highest number of feeder visits occurring from Tufted Titmice and Carolina Chickadees. The first visual sighting of the day was a Carolina Chickadee at 18 minutes before sunrise, while the last was a Carolina Wren just 11 minutes after sunset.

posts.heading: October 5, 2026
posts.text:
The station recorded 16 species and 205 feeder visits, lower than the previous week's average of 19.7 species and 318.9 visits. Eastern Towhees, Blue Jays, and Northern Cardinals were present, while Pileated Woodpeckers, Rose-breasted Grosbeaks, and Ruby-throated Hummingbirds were absent. Eastern Towhees and Carolina Chickadees accounted for the majority of audio detections.

A single Gray Catbird was observed, continuing its presence on six of the last seven days.

Visit counts in the past week fluctuated between 183 and 444. No station changes were recorded after the October 1 feeder installation. The Northern Cardinal was both the first and last bird seen.
